prompt: Your nominal LED calculation calls for a resistor between two available preferred values. You want nominal current no greater than the target. Which is the better next step?

options.text: Choose the lower value because less resistance protects the LED
options.explanation: Less resistance normally increases current for the same source and assumed LED drop.

options.text: Ignore the LED drop and always use the full supply voltage
options.explanation: The resistor takes only the remaining supply voltage in the series model.

options.text: Choose the next higher resistance, then recheck actual current, heat and worst-case limits
options.explanation: Correct. Upward rounding reduces nominal current, but tolerances and voltage variation still need checks.

options.text: Choose either neighbour because resistor value does not affect current
options.explanation: Changing the resistor changes the current-setting path.

workedExample: Use the voltage left after the assumed LED forward drop when selecting the nominal resistance. A higher resistance reduces current under those assumptions. Then check maximum source voltage, minimum LED drop, minimum resistor tolerance, LED/GPIO current limits and resistor dissipation. A nominal target is not a worst-case guarantee.

prompt: An LED itself permits more current than the GPIO pin that drives it. A nominal design already exceeds the pin’s documented limit. What should change?

options.text: Nothing, because only the LED’s rating matters
options.explanation: Both the source pin and LED must operate within their own limits.

options.text: Reduce the drive current or use an appropriate external driver, then check all relevant limits
options.explanation: Correct. The GPIO can be the limiting component even if the LED could carry more current.

options.text: Use a smaller series resistor to protect the pin
options.explanation: A smaller resistance increases current and worsens the overload.

options.text: Keep the circuit because a nominally correct LED voltage guarantees pin safety
options.explanation: Forward voltage is not a current regulator or a guarantee of safe GPIO loading.

workedExample: The current path includes the GPIO, resistor and LED, so every part must be suitable. Reduce current with a properly selected resistor, or use a documented driver if more LED current is needed. Check loaded output voltage, per-pin and combined pin current, tolerances, LED limits and resistor heat; do not treat absolute maximum ratings as targets.
